### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**1** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `os serve (command, 50 pages)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **37** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0c7869c03c9c6ff3a38bd6b09206edeee0184769` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1957932ffa4995ea67e2449c0a45440f9455ab56` — the merge of head `0fb55f6ec76cb38958d4128803e81729e815613f` into base `0c7869c03c9c6ff3a38bd6b09206edeee0184769`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1957932ffa4995ea67e2449c0a45440f9455ab56 && git checkout 1957932ffa4995ea67e2449c0a45440f9455ab56
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0c7869c03c9c6ff3a38bd6b09206edeee0184769 0fb55f6ec76cb38958d4128803e81729e815613f && git checkout -B drift-repro 0c7869c03c9c6ff3a38bd6b09206edeee0184769 && git merge --no-ff 0fb55f6ec76cb38958d4128803e81729e815613f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0c7869c03c9c6ff3a38bd6b09206edeee0184769
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## 席位核对

**L1 verdict: ACCEPT** · PR #34518 · card #34337 · first review · read 2026-11-17T00:14Z

Head-sha: `0fb55f6ec76cb38958d4128803e81729e815613f` (the head named in final-head comment 6933458294)

Read from GitHub at this head (`get_files`, diff, check-runs), not from the report.

**Checklist**
- Shape: draft, base `main`. The body opens with the attribution lines, then `Fixes #34337`. The card's item 3 (document the behaviour if it was intended) is answered in the body as not applicable, so `Fixes` is right. No other card number sits next to a closing verb.
- Scope: 5 files: `cli/src/utils/config.ts` (`stopConfigBundler`), `cli/src/commands/serve.ts` (its one call site), the new integration pin, `scripts/check-cli-test-child-env.mjs`, and a root changeset. The gate file's change is only the census row its own self-test requires for a new built-entry spawner (21 → 22), with the reason written beside it. No `content/docs/releases/`.
- Changeset: root, patch for `@objectstack/cli` (published). I checked each sentence against the diff:
  - "`serve` now stops the esbuild service as soon as the config module has loaded, at boot" matches `await stopConfigBundler()` right after `bundleConfigModule` resolves.
  - "Boots from `--artifact` or `--prebuilt` never started the service and are unchanged" matches the guard `!useArtifactFallback && !flags.prebuilt`, which mirrors the two branches above it that do not bundle.
  - "forward the signal … and exit with the child's code, as before" holds: `start` is not touched.
- Tests: `start-sigterm-process-group.integration.test.ts` spawns the built `bin/run.js` `detached` on a `defineStack` project. It has a positive control (the probe sees `start` and `serve` in the group before the signal), sends SIGTERM to the `start` pid alone, and asserts `kill(-pgid, 0)` answers ESRCH in the exit handler, with exit code 0. The recorded ablation (call removed, CLI rebuilt, `grep -c` = 0 in `dist`) goes red with the `[esbuild] <defunct>` row named; restored and rebuilt, it passes. The integration tier is CI-mandatory (`packages/cli/vitest.config.ts`).
- Gates: 51 check-runs on this head, all `completed`: 35 `success`, 16 `skipped`, 0 failed. Lint & Repo Gates `success`, TypeScript Type Check `success`, Test Core `success`, Check Changeset `success`.

**Spot checks (mine)**
1. Nothing else in `serve` uses esbuild after boot: at this head, `serve.ts`'s only esbuild path is the one `bundleConfigModule` call, and it is awaited before `stop()`, so no in-flight build is cut. `loadConfig` is imported but not called there. A later esbuild call in the same process would start a fresh service; `stop()` does not disable esbuild.
2. Same instance: `bundle-require` (`^5.1.0`) takes esbuild as a peer, and `@objectstack/cli` declares `esbuild` `^0.28.2`, so the dynamic `import('esbuild')` resolves the copy the bundler ran. The built-entry pin is the measured proof of that on this workspace.
3. The premise table in the body was measured on `origin/main` before the change. The `--artifact` row is already clean there, which agrees with the guard skipping those boots.

**L2 owed: no.** None of the four contract faces is touched: `Clause-②: no`, no narrowing, no `packages/spec/src/**` path, no governed rule text (`scripts/*.mjs` is not on the governed register).

**Landing tier**: `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 34518` reports NOT governed, +260/−2 = 262 lines ≤ 3000. Ordinary queue landing by the area at this head.
